decisions.context: Cameras inspect production-line images where network access is often unavailable. The detection path must still work locally.

alternatives.label: On-device inference
cons: Small team: device fleet to support

decisions.rationale: Network independence decides the choice because inspections must work without connectivity. This gives up simpler centralized runtime management and requires capable devices.
consequences: Each device needs suitable compute and local model storage.
Inference can continue during network outages.

decisions.decision: Package each model as a versioned release
decisions.context: The model is retrained weekly and pushed to production devices. Releases need a clear identity so teams can tell which model a device is running and reproduce a deployment.

alternatives.label: Versioned model artifact with training metadata
pros: Reproducibility: ties model to training inputs and settings
cons: Weekly model updates: requires release packaging work

alternatives.label: Replace the model file in place
cons: Small team: harder to diagnose device differences

chosen.label: Versioned model artifact with training metadata

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides the choice: the team needs to identify and recreate weekly releases. This costs extra packaging effort for each update.
consequences: Each release must retain its model and associated training metadata.
Devices and deployment records need to identify the release version.

decisions.decision: Distribute releases through an update service with device-side staging
decisions.context: Updated models must reach cameras that may be offline. A device needs a safe way to accept a release when it reconnects without interrupting inspection.

alternatives.label: Device-initiated update with staged activation
pros: Network independence: updates can wait until reconnect
Inspection continuity: activate after local staging
cons: Small team: needs update and state handling

alternatives.label: Central server push with immediate replacement
pros: Weekly model updates: direct rollout control
cons: Inspection continuity: replacement can interrupt inspection

decisions.rationale: Network independence decides the choice because devices cannot be assumed reachable at rollout time. Staging adds update logic and delays adoption on disconnected devices.
consequences: Devices need local storage for staged releases.
Update status may differ across devices until they reconnect.

decisions.decision: Retain labelled images and training inputs as a reproducible dataset snapshot
decisions.context: Newly labelled images drive weekly retraining. Preserving the inputs used for each release supports reproduction and investigation of model changes.

alternatives.label: Snapshot training inputs per release
pros: Weekly model updates: supports release comparison
cons: Infrastructure cost: stores repeated data or snapshots

alternatives.label: Train from a mutable latest dataset
cons: Reproducibility: inputs can change after training
Weekly model updates: comparisons become ambiguous

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides the choice because weekly model behavior should be traceable to its labelled inputs. This uses additional storage and retention effort.
consequences: Each model release needs a reference to its dataset snapshot.
Storage requirements grow with retained snapshots.
